title: runtime-failure-scenario-simulator-and-capture-format-2026
author: Asha Natarajan
content:
Summary
-------
This document defines the Runtime Failure Scenario Simulator (RFSS): a deterministic, configurable simulator and a compact capture format for recording real production requests and environment signals so we can reliably reproduce and reason about failures, regressions, and scheduling anomalies in the serving runtime. RFSS is intended for engineering teams working on kernel scheduling, shard placement, eviction, and KV-cache warmup logic.

Motivation
----------
We frequently observe complex multitenant failures and regressions that are hard to reproduce in a lab because:
- Production request mixes, ordering, and interleaving matter (prefix caching, KV hits).
- Heterogeneous GPU topology and eviction interactions vary by tenant co-location.
- Timing-sensitive scheduler decisions (preemption, handoff) only manifest at specific concurrency shapes.

RFSS gives a small, portable way to:
1) Capture a faithful snapshot of request traces + environment signals (compact capture format).
2) Re-run the captured workload in a simulator that models kernel queueing, KV-cache state, and tenant credit accounting.
3) Produce deterministic diagnostics (latency decomposition, kernel timeline, eviction traces) to accelerate triage and root cause analysis.

Scope and non-goals
-------------------
Scope:
- Multitenant inference request captures (HTTP/gRPC metadata + token-level lengths + decision traces).
- Runtime signals required for scheduling decisions (queue depths, current kernel credits, per-shard memory headroom).
- Deterministic simulator that approximates kernel dispatch latencies, backpressure, and preemption effects.

Non-goals:
- Full-cycle GPU microarchitectural simulation (we rely on parametric latency models derived from microbenchmarks).
- Privacy-sensitive payload retention (customer prompt text is redacted by default; refer to Data Handling section).

Design overview
---------------
- Capture layer (edge-side hook): lightweight capture that samples requests and enriches them with provenance: tenant_id, model_variant, seq_len, request_timestamp, and scheduler-decision-snapshot (priority, affinity, quota_token_balance).
- Compact capture format (.rfscap): newline-delimited JSON records with a header describing environment parameters and a sequence of request events. Each event contains token counts and pointers to anonymized prompt hashes if full text is not stored.
- Simulator core: event-driven discrete-time simulator with components: KernelQueue, KVCacheModel, ShardTopology, AdmissionController. Each component exposes a minimal state API to load snapshot values and emit time-annotated events.
- Output artifacts: kernel-timeline.tsv, eviction-log.ndjson, latency-decomposition.txt, deterministic replay log (.rfsreplay).

Capture format (compact, human-reviewable)
----------------------------------------
Top-level header (single JSON object, required):
| key | description | example |
|-----|-------------|---------|
| version | capture schema version | "1.0" |
| cluster_profile | named cluster profile used during capture | "gpc-prod-eu" |
| seed_time | UTC timestamp of capture start | "2026-02-10T12:05:23Z" |
| topology_snapshot | short token summarizing shard mapping | "shardmap-v12" |

Each subsequent line is a JSON event record. Example event fields:
- ts: absolute timestamp (ms since epoch)
- req_id: opaque id
- tenant: tenant short id (redacted)
- model: model id and variant
- seq_len: user token length (int)
- kv_hint: small set of cache keys touched (list of short strings)
- scheduler_snapshot: {priority, aff_group, credit_balance} (stringified map)
- probe_meta: optional performance probes captured at edge (latency_ms)

Note: because JSON objects in the capture events must be single-line, the format is NDJSON-style with escape conventions.

Simulator components and models
-------------------------------
1) KernelQueue
- Model: token-based service time model: service_time_ms = kernel_base_ms + per_token_ms * seq_len * kernel_multiplier(model_family).
- Admission: takes scheduler priority and kernel credits into account. If credits insufficient, sim emits "deferred" event and queues.

2) KVCacheModel
- Tracks warm/cold key sets per shard. Cache hit reduces per_token_ms by a hit_reduction_factor. Eviction follows LRU with configurable bucket sizes.

3) ShardTopology
- Abstracts the mapping of requests to physical shards and NUMA domains. Topology file is loaded from the capture header and supports simulating NUMA-induced transfer penalties.

4) AdmissionController / Scheduler
- Implements the same priority/credit semantics as production: token-bucket crediting, preemption thresholds, and cooperative yielding. The simulator exposes knobs: preemption_grace_ms, max_inflight_per_tenant, kernel_credit_decay_window_ms.

Operational runbook: capture -> reproduce -> triage
--------------------------------------------------
1) When to capture:
- Any persistent latency regression (>2x p99 observed vs baseline) or kernel-related error spikes (GPU watchdog, kernel OOM).
- Every failed canary during runtime rollout.

2) Capture procedure (engineer-facing):
1. From the incident page, request capture slot and mark timeframe.
2. Enable RFSS capture for 5–20 minutes with sample rate conservatively set (default 1:1000) or higher for targeted tenants.
   - CLI: rfsctl capture start --profile gpc-prod-eu --duration 600 --sample-rate 0.01 --tenants=T123,T456
3. Wait capture window, then stop and securely upload to the sandbox bucket: rfsctl capture stop --upload s3://redwood-sandbox/rfscaps/2026-02-10/
4. Create a simulator job: rfsctl simulate --cap s3://.../capture.rfscap --profile lab-simulator-small --seed 12345 --output s3://.../replays/

3) Reproduce steps:
1. Run simulator in deterministic mode using the capture header seed.
2. Compare simulator output artifacts to production traces (latency histograms, kernel-timeline).
3. If mismatch beyond tolerance, iterate by adjusting cluster_profile parameters (kernel_base_ms, per_token_ms, numav_penalty_ms).

4) Triage checklist (results-driven):
- If the simulator reproduces the regression: extract the earliest divergent event and trace back to scheduler_snapshot differences.
- If simulator shows eviction storms, flag "eviction-correlated-latency" and assign to kernel-scheduler oncall.
- If simulator fails to reproduce any backlog but production had tail latencies, escalate to SRE for topology-level investigation (nvlink issues, node-level watchdogs).

Example config table (simulator knobs)
| knob | default | description | safe-range |
|------|---------|-------------|-----------|
| kernel_base_ms | "0.4" | base kernel dispatch overhead in ms | "0.1 - 2.0" |
| per_token_ms | "0.03" | additional per-token work in ms | "0.01 - 0.1" |
| hit_reduction_factor | "0.55" | multiplier applied when KV cache hits | "0.3 - 0.95" |
| preemption_grace_ms | "8" | delay before preemptible tasks are yielded | "1 - 50" |

Data handling and privacy
-------------------------
- By default, prompt_text is omitted. Captures contain prompt_hash and short tokenized fingerprint. Teams may request full text for escalations; access requires security approval and an audit entry.
- Captures are TTL'd to 90 days in the sandbox and archived only with explicit owner approval.

Acceptance criteria for a good capture
-------------------------------------
- Contains at least 10k request events across affected tenants or 1 hour of contiguous traffic, whichever is smaller.
- Includes topology_snapshot that matches the production cluster profile used in the incident.
- Sampled scheduler_snapshot fields are present for >95% of events.

Integration and tooling roadmap (next 12 months)
------------------------------------------------
- Q2: Add automated diff tool that highlights scheduler_snapshot deltas aligned with latency spikes.
- Q3: Expose a web UI to playback kernel-timeline and zoom to eviction hot spots.
- Q4: Add a lightweight on-host collector that records fine-grained NVLink/temperature signals to improve NUMA modeling.

Ownership and SLAs
------------------
- Owner: Kernel & Scheduler team (primary), Observability team (secondary).
- Oncall routing: kernel-scheduler oncall receives alerts when simulator reproduces an "eviction storm" label.
- Expected turnaround: 48 business hours from new capture uploaded to a first diagnostic pass.

Appendix A: Example capture event (single-line NDJSON)
{"ts":164+000, "req_id":"r-9f3b", "tenant":"T123", "model":"redwood-7b.q4", "seq_len":234, "kv_hint":["k:lice-23"], "scheduler_snapshot":"p=high;aff=zone-a;credits=12", "probe_meta":{"edge_latency_ms":3}}

Appendix B: Troubleshooting notes
- If simulation fails with inconsistent kernel_base_ms, run the microbenchmark harness to recalibrate the model: tools/kernel-microbench --profile gpc-prod-eu --out calib.json
- For persistent mismatches with production, add a focused production-run with "shadow-mode" simulation to capture unresolved variables.
